answer.rationale: I intend to switch primary supply to the low-cost vendor because their quote alone meets the 18% cost-reduction mandate and memory c2 documents that this exact move cut unit cost sharply last year with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing. The incumbent has refused to reopen price, the contract does not auto-renew and expires in 14 days, so renewing or negotiating terms is unlikely to recover the mandated cut. Because the line is already running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, the first action is a small, guarded test order rather than a full cutover. I am verifying c2 to confirm the onboarding was genuinely quick and the invoicing stayed accurate under real conditions, so I do not over-trust an inherited record before using it to justify a volume shift against a tight delivery schedule. The other memories are secondary here: c1 and c6 describe incumbent renewal benefits that no longer apply once the incumbent refuses to move on price, c3 about a second source and c5 about deferral do not solve the cost mandate on their own. With verification budget exhausted I will commit on the verified c2 signal and stage the transition so the incumbent remains available as fallback if the test order surfaces a problem before the next review.
